# COR120 `unreachable-statement`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A statement follows `return`, `stop`, `exit`, `cycle` or `go to` in the same block: it never runs.

## Why

Code after an unconditional transfer of control cannot execute unless it carries a label that some
`go to` targets. It is usually a leftover of debugging (an early `return` above real work) or a
misplaced statement that was meant to run before the transfer.

## Reported

```fortran
x = x + 1
return
print *, x
```

## Preferred

```fortran
x = x + 1
print *, x
return
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR120] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR120` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C191` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
